author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Somerville firefighters rescued a resident from a three-story apartment building after a fire broke out on Dartmouth Street shortly before 3 a.m. Monday, Boston 25 News reported.

Crews arrived to heavy flames on the first floor. A resident of that unit had already escaped by jumping and was treated for injuries described as not life-threatening. Firefighters then moved through heavy smoke to reach and remove a resident from the second floor.

Two cats were also rescued from the building. The report did not specify how many residents were displaced or provide an estimate of the property damage. Officials were continuing to investigate what started the fire.

The response closed off part of the neighborhood while crews worked inside the building and checked for remaining occupants. No firefighter injuries were reported in the initial account. Residents should rely on Somerville fire officials for any later findings about the cause, building access or assistance for people affected.
dek: Crews entered heavy smoke to remove a second-floor resident after another occupant escaped by jumping from the burning building.
headline: Somerville firefighters rescue resident from apartment blaze
